column1: # Console functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Writes values to the console, then a new line unless it ends with a comma or semicolon.
Writes values formatted by a template such as "##.##" or "&".
Writes values separated by commas, with strings in double quotes.
Skips a number of columns inside a Print, leaving those cells unchanged.
Moves to a column inside a Print, on the next line if already past it.
Reads values the user types, up to Enter, after an optional prompt.
Reads a whole typed line into a string, commas included, after an optional prompt.
Returns the next key waiting, or an empty string at once if there is none.
Waits for a key and returns its code; the key is not shown on screen.
Waits for a number of characters from the keyboard or a file and returns them.
Reads a number of wide characters from a file or device and returns them.
Clears the screen, or only the text or graphics viewport.
Moves the text cursor to a row and column, and can show or hide it.
Returns the row the cursor is on, counting from 1 at the top.
Returns the column the cursor is in, counting from 1 at the left.
Sets the colours for text printed from now on, and returns the previous ones.
Sets or returns the number of columns and rows of the console.
Limits printing and scrolling to a range of rows, or to the whole screen again.
Returns the character, or its colour, at a row and column of the console.
Holds your app: you write Init to set up, Update to react and View to draw.
Sets up your app and returns its first command, such as a tick to start animating.
Reacts to one event and returns what the loop should do next; it never draws.
Draws the whole screen from your app's state, changing nothing.
Runs once as the loop ends, while the terminal is still taken.
Runs your app full-screen and restores the terminal; returns the exit code or an error.
Holds loop settings: frames per second and whether Ctrl+C quits.
Returns the default loop settings: 60 frames per second, quit on Ctrl+C.
Holds which terminal features to take: alternate screen, raw keys, mouse and more.
Returns the usual terminal settings, with the mouse and focus events left off.
Holds one event: a key, mouse action, resize, paste, focus change or tick.
Holds a key press: a character or a named key, plus Shift, Ctrl and Alt.
Returns true if the key is a typed character rather than a named key.
Returns true if the given modifier, Shift, Alt or Ctrl, was held.
Returns a readable name for a key, such as "Ctrl+Shift+F5".
Holds a mouse event: press, release, move or wheel, the button, and the cell.
Holds a command for the loop: what to do, plus a delay or an exit code.
Returns a command that does nothing, for events your app ignores.
Returns a command that draws the next frame; only the cells that changed are sent.
Returns a command that ends the loop, so TuiRun returns the given exit code.
Returns a command that sends one tick event after a delay; return another to repeat.
Returns a command that repaints the whole screen instead of only the changes.
Returns a command that leaves the terminal, suspends the program, then comes back.
Returns a clock in milliseconds that never goes backwards, the one the loop uses.
Draws a border with titles and an optional fill; Inner gives the space inside.
Adds a title to one side of the border, aligned left, centre or right.
Returns the space inside the border, which is empty for a very small block.
Holds one title on a block's border: its text, style and alignment.
Returns a title value; the side argument comes before the alignment.
Returns the characters for a border kind, such as plain ASCII for older consoles.
Holds the six characters a border is drawn from: two lines and four corners.
Draws text, wrapped or not, aligned left, centre or right, and scrollable.
Draws a one-row strip of tab titles with the selected one highlighted.
Draws a progress bar for a ratio from 0 to 1, labelled with the percentage.
Draws a bar filled to a ratio whose colour shades from one end to the other.
Draws a busy indicator that moves on one step each time you call Advance.
Moves the spinner to its next frame, wrapping at the end.
Fills an array with the default braille spinner frames.
Draws a scrolling list the user moves through with the arrow keys.
Holds a list's selected item and scroll position; -1 means nothing is selected.
Draws a scrolling table with headers, its columns sized like a layout.
Holds a table's selected row and scroll position.
Holds one table row: its cell texts in column order.
Draws a tree of nodes that the user expands and collapses with the arrow keys.
Appends a node at a depth; the deeper nodes after it become its children.
Counts the nodes currently shown, leaving out those inside collapsed nodes.
Holds one tree node: its label, depth, whether it has children, and your own id.
Holds a tree's selected node and scroll position.
Draws a scrollbar from a total, the number visible and the current position.
Draws a one-line text box with a cursor, selection and optional password masking.
Holds a text box's text, cursor, selection and scroll position.
Sets a text box's state to empty with nothing selected; call it before first use.
Inserts text at the cursor, replacing any selection first.
Removes the selected text, or does nothing if none is selected.
Returns where the selection starts, or the cursor position if nothing is selected.
Returns where the selection ends, or the cursor position if nothing is selected.
Draws a multi-line text editor with optional line numbers.
Holds a text area's lines, cursor line and column, and scroll position.
Sets a text area's state to one empty line; call it before first use.
Draws a labelled checkbox that Space or Enter toggles, changing your own boolean.
Draws a set of options where one is chosen, stored in your own variable.
Draws a dropdown list of options that opens over whatever is below it.
Returns true if the dropdown's list is showing.
Holds a dropdown's chosen option, whether it is open, and the highlighted entry.
Draws a button that calls your procedure when the user presses Enter on it.
Draws a button whose handler is a lambda that captures variables.
Holds the Tab order of your widgets and tells each one when it has focus.
Adds a widget to the end of the Tab order; the widget must outlive the frame.
Moves focus to the next widget, wrapping at the end, as Tab does.
Moves focus to the previous widget, wrapping at the start, as Shift+Tab does.
Focuses a given widget, or returns false if it is not in the ring.
Returns the focused widget, or no value if the ring is empty.
Counts the widgets in the Tab order.
Empties the Tab order; the widgets themselves are left alone.
Draws a floating panel over the screen, optionally modal and dimming what is behind.
Draws a dialog with a title, a message and buttons, coloured by its kind.
Returns true once Enter was pressed on a button; selected says which.
Returns true once the dialog was dismissed with Esc.
Draws a one-row menu bar whose menus drop down with Enter.
Returns true if one of the menus is dropped down.
Holds one menu of a menu bar: its label and its items.
Draws one row of status items, some packed to the left and some to the right.
Adds an item at the left or right; include any padding spaces in the text.
Holds one status bar item: its text, style and alignment.
Returns a status bar item from text, a style and an alignment.
Draws a line graph of one or more series, scaled to fit or to a fixed range.
Holds one line of a graph: its values, newest last, plus a colour and name.
Draws a one-row trend of values as block characters, one value per cell.
Draws labelled bars, vertical or horizontal, scaled to the largest value.
Holds one bar of a bar chart: its label, value and colour.
Holds a braille drawing surface with a grid of 2 by 4 dots in every cell.
Sets one dot in a colour; a dot outside the canvas is ignored.
Draws a straight line of dots between two points.
Turns every dot off.
Draws the canvas into an area of the frame as braille characters.
Changes the canvas size in cells and clears it.
Returns the canvas width in cells.
Returns the canvas height in cells.
Returns the canvas width in dots, two per cell.
Returns the canvas height in dots, four per cell.
Returns the braille dot pattern of one cell as a byte.
Splits a rectangle into rows stacked top to bottom, sized by constraints.
Splits a rectangle into columns side by side, sized by constraints.
Returns a constraint for exactly n cells.
Returns a constraint that shares the space left over, by weight.
Returns a constraint for a percentage of the whole space being split.
Returns a constraint for a fraction of the whole space, such as one third.
Returns a constraint for at least n cells, more if there is room.
Returns a constraint for at most n cells.
Holds one sizing rule for a split, such as a fixed length or a share of the rest.
Returns the sizes that constraints give a total, adding up to exactly that total.
Returns a rectangle of a given size centred in another, as for a dialog.
Returns a rectangle of a given width at the left, centre or right of another.
Returns a rectangle shrunk by a margin.
Returns a rectangle shrunk by the same amount on every side.
Holds child widgets laid out in a row or column; it deletes them when it goes.
Adds a child widget made with New and the constraint that sizes it.
Returns the rectangle a child got at the last Render, for mouse hit tests.
Holds a rectangle of cells: x, y, width and height, counted from 0.
Returns a rectangle from x, y, width and height.
Returns true if a cell is inside the rectangle; use it to hit-test the mouse.
Returns the overlap of two rectangles, or an empty one if they do not touch.
Returns the rectangle shrunk by a margin, empty rather than negative.
Returns true if the rectangle has no width or no height.
Returns true if two rectangles have the same position and size.
Returns x plus the width: the first column past the right edge.
Returns y plus the height: the first row below the bottom edge.
Holds a cell position: x and y.
Holds a size in columns and rows.
Returns a size from columns and rows.
Holds an inset for each side, in the order left, top, right, bottom.
Returns a margin from left, top, right and bottom.
Returns a margin of the same size on every side.
Holds a text style: colours, attributes such as bold, and which of them it sets.
Returns a style with a foreground, a background and optional attributes.
Returns a partial style that sets only the parts you name, such as just bold.
Returns the terminal's default style: default colours and no attributes.
Returns this style with another laid over it, keeping whatever the other leaves unset.
Returns true if the style has an attribute such as bold or underline.
Returns true if two styles are identical, including which parts they set.
Holds twelve named styles, such as normal, accent, selected and danger.
Returns the stock colour theme.
Returns a theme made from bold, dim, reverse and underline, with no colours.
Holds a colour: the terminal's default, one of 16 or 256, or 24-bit RGB.
Returns a 24-bit colour, reduced for you on terminals with fewer colours.
Returns one of the 16 classic colours, which follow the user's terminal theme.
Returns a colour from the 256-colour palette by its number.
Returns the terminal's own default colour; as a background it does not paint.
Returns the classic black, palette colour 0.
Returns the classic red, palette colour 1.
Returns the classic green, palette colour 2.
Returns the classic yellow, palette colour 3.
Returns the classic blue, palette colour 4.
Returns the classic magenta, palette colour 5.
Returns the classic cyan, palette colour 6.
Returns the classic white, palette colour 7.
Returns the classic bright black, palette colour 8.
Returns the classic bright red, palette colour 9.
Returns the classic bright green, palette colour 10.
Returns the classic bright yellow, palette colour 11.
Returns the classic bright blue, palette colour 12.
Returns the classic bright magenta, palette colour 13.
Returns the classic bright cyan, palette colour 14.
Returns the classic bright white, palette colour 15.
Returns true if two colours were built the same way with the same values.
Returns the palette number of a 16-colour or 256-colour value.
Returns true if the colour is the terminal's own default.
Returns a colour part of the way between two others, for t from 0 to 1.
Returns the colour that a terminal with fewer colours would show instead.
Returns a style with both its colours reduced to what a terminal can show.
Returns the nearest 256-palette colour number for red, green and blue values.
Returns the nearest of the 16 classic colours for red, green and blue values.
Returns how bright a colour looks, from 0.0 to 1.0.
Counts the columns a string takes on screen, wide characters as two.
Returns the columns one character takes: 0, 1 or 2.
Cuts a string to fit a number of columns, ending in "..." unless you pass "".
Breaks text into lines that fit a number of columns, keeping its line breaks.
Sets whether characters of ambiguous width count as two columns, for CJK terminals.
Returns true if characters of ambiguous width count as two columns.
Holds the surface View draws on; drawing never fails and is clipped to fit.
Returns the whole screen as a rectangle at 0, 0, the start of every layout.
Draws a string at a cell and returns the number of columns it used.
Writes one character cell, replacing the style that was there.
Fills a rectangle with one character in one style.
Lays a style over every cell of a rectangle, keeping the characters.
Returns the rectangle that drawing is currently limited to.
Limits drawing to a rectangle and returns the previous limit, to restore later.
Restores the drawing limit that PushClip returned.
Starts an overlay layer, as a popup or an open dropdown uses.
Ends the overlay layer that PushLayer started.
Shows the text cursor at a cell for this frame.
Hides the text cursor for this frame, which is the default.
Returns true if this frame asked to show the cursor.
Returns the cell where the cursor was last put.
Holds the base type every widget extends; you write Render and Kind for your own.
Draws the widget into an area of the frame, changing no app state.
Offers an event to the widget and returns true if the widget used it.
Returns the widget's short type name, such as "Block".
Returns true if the widget can take focus; false unless it is interactive.
Tells the widget whether it has focus; the focus ring calls it for you.
Returns the size the widget would like in the space given; layouts may ignore it.
Runs Init and View once with no terminal and returns the bytes it would write.
Holds two cell buffers and works out the bytes that turn one frame into the next.
Clears the back buffer and returns the frame to draw into.
Returns the bytes that change the last frame into the new one, then swaps buffers.
Changes the screen size in cells and forces a full repaint.
Makes the next Render clear and repaint the whole screen.
Returns the screen width in cells.
Returns the screen height in cells.
Returns the buffer being drawn into, so a test can read its cells.
Returns the buffer the terminal is taken to show: the last frame sent.
Holds a grid of character cells, stored row by row.
Returns a pointer to the cell at x, y, without checking the bounds.
Returns true if x, y is inside the buffer.
Fills every cell with a space in the given style.
Changes the grid size and blanks every cell.
Returns the number of cells: columns times rows.
Holds one character cell: the character, its style and its width in columns.
Sets the cell's character and works out its width in columns.
Returns true if two cells have the same character, style and width.
Returns a cell holding a space in the given style.
Holds the terminal itself, for writing your own loop: modes, size and output.
Takes over the terminal with the options asked for; fails if output is not a terminal.
Puts the terminal back the way Enter found it; safe to call more than once.
Returns true between a successful Enter and its Leave.
Returns the terminal's size in columns and rows, or an error if it reports none.
Returns true once after each resize of the terminal, then false.
Adds bytes to the output buffer; nothing is sent until Flush.
Adds a string to the output buffer as UTF-8.
Sends the buffered output in one write and empties the buffer.
Throws the buffered output away without sending it.
Counts the bytes buffered and not yet sent.
Returns what the terminal can do, as detected once when it was entered.
Detects what the terminal can do again, without entering it.
Holds what a terminal can do: colour depth, mouse, paste, focus events, Unicode.
Holds a terminal error: a code and what was being attempted.
Returns a readable line saying what failed, including any system error number.
Holds the parser that turns raw terminal bytes into events.
Adds raw bytes from the terminal; an unfinished sequence is kept for later.
Returns the next complete event, or no value yet; a lone Esc waits for a timeout.
Adds an event to the back of the queue, to inject input yourself.
Counts the parsed events waiting to be taken.
Counts the bytes held that do not yet make a whole event.
Throws away the held bytes and the queued events.
Returns true if the parser holds an Esc it cannot yet tell from a key sequence.
Returns the escape sequence that Enter writes for a set of options.
Returns the escape sequence that Leave writes to undo those options.
Returns the escape sequence that clears the terminal screen.
Returns the escape sequence that moves the cursor to a cell counted from 0.
Returns the escape sequence that shows or hides the cursor.
Returns the escape sequence that changes the terminal from one style to another.
Returns the escape sequence that resets every colour and attribute.
Returns the Windows console input mode that Enter would set for given options.
